#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail

SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
ROOT="$(git -C "$SCRIPT_ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$SCRIPT_ROOT")"
export EOS_ROOT="$ROOT"

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf 'ERROR: python3 is required by the repository-local EOS control tooling.\n' >&2
  exit 127
fi

CANONICAL="$ROOT/tools/eos/canonical_state.py"
LEGACY="$ROOT/tools/eos/eos.py"

# Canonical-state administration is handled directly by the state controller.
if [[ "${1:-}" == "state" ]]; then
  shift
  exec python3 "$CANONICAL" "$@"
fi

# `rebuild-state` historically treated the event ledger as the current-state
# authority. Under the single-canonical-state model it is retained as a
# compatibility alias for projecting the canonical snapshot.
if [[ "${1:-}" == "rebuild-state" ]]; then
  shift
  printf 'NOTE: rebuild-state now projects from .eos/state/current.json (canonical).\n' >&2
  exec python3 "$CANONICAL" project "$@"
fi

# Every legacy EOS command runs inside a canonical transaction:
# 1. fail closed if any projection already drifted;
# 2. let the compatibility runtime operate on generated projections;
# 3. capture only a successful, internally consistent mutation into canonical
#    machine-readable state; otherwise canonical state never advances.
python3 "$CANONICAL" pre -- "$@"

set +e
python3 "$LEGACY" "$@"
rc=$?
set -e

if (( rc != 0 )); then
  rm -f "$ROOT/.eos/cache/canonical-state-transaction.json"
  exit "$rc"
fi

python3 "$CANONICAL" post -- "$@"
case "${1:-}" in
  preflight|worktree|execute|execution|contract|codex)
    exec python3 "$ROOT/tools/eos/execution_v2.py" "$@"
    ;;
  validate|validators|validation|evidence|performance|security|supply-chain|verify)
    exec python3 "$ROOT/tools/eos/verification_v2.py" "$@"
    ;;
  *)
    exec python3 "$ROOT/tools/eos/eos.py" "$@"
    ;;
esac
